title: In the news: Quad research earns national media coverage
summary: New research from Quad and The Harris Poll is sparking media conversations about digital fatigue, human connection and the future of shopping.
body_markdown:
In an increasingly digital world, American consumers are looking for more human elements in their shopping experiences. Led by Gen Z, the first digitally native generation, the shift is driven by mounting fatigue with endless scrolling and constant screen time. Across generations, consumers are rebalancing toward human-centered, in-store experiences and want shopping to feel more social, tactile and full of discovery.


Quad recently released


[Return of Touch: The Human Advantage](https://www.quad.com/engage/the-return-of-touch) , its latest consumer research with The Harris Poll. The study puts numbers behind this shift and points to clear opportunities for consumer-facing brands:


- **


75% of Americans say a simpler relationship with technology feels like a lifestyle upgrade rather than a sacrifice.


- **


80% say brands that feel human and imperfect stick with them more than brands focused on AI-generated perfection.


- **


84% of Gen Z say they have gone out of their way for an in-person shopping experience.


### Since its release, the research has sparked media conversations, including coverage from:


- **


**Fast Company:**[Gen Z is bringing back something the digital age was supposed to replace](https://www.fastcompany.com/91625146/gen-z-is-bringing-back-something-the-digital-age-was-supposed-to-replace) , which explores Gen Z’s growing interest in offline activities,


collectibles


and physical experiences.


- **


**Forbes:**[AI Fatigue Is Turning Human Touch Into a Marketing Advantage](https://www.forbes.com/sites/gabrielalinzainescu/2026/10/20/ai-fatigue-is-turning-human-touch-into-a-marketing-advantage/) , which examines what the findings mean for trust, print,


packaging


and in-store experiences.


- **


**EMARKETER:**[Consumers’ digital fatigue creates new opportunities for in-store brand experiences](https://www.emarketer.com/content/consumers-digital-fatigue-creates-new-opportunities-in-store-brand-experiences) , which highlights the growing appeal of destination shopping and physical brand experiences.


- **


**Fortune:**[Millennials are ‘kidulting’ through their parenthood stage](https://fortune.com/2026/10/20/millennials-kidulting-harris-poll-nostalgia-blind-box-arcade-claw/) , which cites the research in its examination of nostalgia, collecting and the desire for something physical.


To learn more about how consumers are rethinking technology,


shopping


and real-world connection, and what these shifts mean for marketers, explore


[The Human Advantage data sheet](https://www.quad.com/engage/the-return-of-touch-2026-data-sheet) .
